verdict.rationale: LangSmith's docs say you can 'automate workflows with rules, webhooks, and online evaluations.' Threshold alerts with stackable filter conditions route to any HTTP endpoint via webhook, and online evaluators run automatically on production traces with filters and sampling. Together these give user-defined conditions that trigger actions automatically. Missing for 10: detailed docs on what actions automation rules can take (e.g., adding traces to datasets or annotation queues), and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Automate workflows with rules, webhooks, and online evaluations.
Alerts can route to Slack, PagerDuty, Dynatrace, or any HTTP endpoint via webhook.
for Errors and Latency, you can use the filter builder to stack conditions on fields such as Status, Run Type, Tag, and Error.
Set up evaluators to run automatically on production traces: safety checks, format validation, quality heuristics, and reference-free LLM-as-judge. Apply filters and sampling rates to control costs.
